title: Project Overview
description: Start here. The README (originally in Chinese) frames Self-Agent as an enterprise AI Agent built on LangGraph 1.x, MCP, A2A, and a multi-protocol LLM abstraction covering GLM, OpenAI, and Anthropic. It documents the three delivery modes (a React web chat, a Python CLI coding agent, and direct REST access) and the five-minute quick start built around the docker-compose stack. Read it to absorb the project's purpose and the component vocabulary that the rest of this tour expands on.

title: Application Composition Root
description: app/main.py is the FastAPI composition root: its lifespan context is where every subsystem is born (the database pool, the MCP client, the tool and skill registries, the memory store, the compiled LangGraph, and the A2A mount) before routers, exception handlers, rate-limit and metrics middleware, and OpenTelemetry are attached. Beside it, app/core/config.py is the single pydantic-settings source of truth, where every environment variable maps one-to-one to a Settings field. Treat these two files as the map of the whole server: anything main.py imports is a subsystem you will visit in a later step.
languageLesson: FastAPI's lifespan async context manager replaces the old on_event('startup') hooks: yield separates the setup phase (before the app serves traffic) from teardown (run on shutdown), so DB pools, MCP clients, and the compiled graph are guaranteed ready before the first request.

title: Core Foundation
description: These cross-cutting modules are depended on by almost everything; logging.py has the highest fan-in in the entire codebase. logging.py injects the OpenTelemetry trace ID into every log line; exceptions.py defines the AppError hierarchy and the uniform JSON error envelope that hides details in production; telemetry.py configures OTLP exporters and the GenAI semantic-convention span helpers used throughout the agent; and db/manager.py is the lazy lifecycle owner of all four databases (Postgres, MongoDB, Redis, Neo4j). They are intentionally boring and ubiquitous, which is exactly why understanding them early pays off.
languageLesson: OpenTelemetry context propagation: the trace ID set by telemetry.py is captured per-log-record via a logging Filter that reads from otel's active context, so every log line in a distributed request stays correlatable to its span in Jaeger.

title: The Agent Brain
description: This is the heart of the project. agent/graph.py assembles the LangGraph StateGraph as a hand-written ReAct loop (agent_node to tools_node, looping, with a checkpointer) rather than the library's create_react_agent, deliberately to keep full control of the multi-protocol LLM layer from Step 5. agent/state.py defines the AgentState TypedDict (the graph's state schema) using an add_messages reducer for history and a custom replace_plan reducer for the task plan. agent/nodes/agent_node.py is the LLM-calling node: it streams tokens, opens a GenAI span, and returns either a reply or a batch of tool_calls for the next step.
languageLesson: LangGraph reducers: when a node returns state, each key is merged via its declared reducer rather than overwritten. add_messages appends or updates by message id; a custom reducer lets the plan field be wholesale-replaced so tools can mutate the task plan atomically.

title: Multi-Protocol LLM Abstraction
description: To let one agent speak to GLM, OpenAI, and Anthropic behind a single API, this layer defines a provider-agnostic contract. llm/base.py declares LLMClient as a runtime-checkable Protocol (chat and stream_chat); llm/models.py holds the unified Pydantic models (ChatRequest, ChatMessage, tool calls, usage, stream chunks) that every provider converts to and from; llm/factory.py builds and lru-caches the right client from settings (GLM and OpenAI share the OpenAI-compatible client); and providers/openai_like.py is that shared implementation, including the tricky cross-chunk aggregation of streamed tool calls. This seam is what the agent_node from Step 4 calls; it never sees a vendor SDK directly.
languageLesson: typing.Protocol with @runtime_checkable verifies structural conformance via isinstance without inheritance, so a provider is 'an LLMClient' purely by having the right methods and properties; no base class coupling is required.

title: Tool Execution & Safe Coding Toolkit
description: When the agent decides to act, control passes to this group. tools_node.py executes the agent's tool_calls concurrently but routes destructive ones through a LangGraph interrupt so a human can approve them before they run. The built-in coding tools (files.py for read/write/edit/grep and shell.py for command execution) never touch absolute paths or a raw shell directly: workspace.py confines every path to a project root with .gitignore-aware ignore matching and sensitive-file guards, and sandbox.py wraps shell commands in Linux Landlock and bubblewrap confinement (filesystem jail, network block, private tmp). Together they are why the CLI can operate on your real disk safely.
languageLesson: LangGraph interrupt() suspends the graph and resumes it after human input; the persisted checkpointer state survives the pause, so an approval round-trip can even outlive a process restart. The tool registry classifies each tool's risk tier to decide which calls trigger an interrupt.

title: Three-Tier Memory System
description: Memory here is layered. checkpointer.py selects the LangGraph short-term state backend (MemorySaver for dev, AsyncPostgresSaver for production); this is what lets a thread pause for approval in Step 6 and resume, or be replayed. store.py is the long-term cross-session store (AsyncPostgresStore with a vector index) exposed through a MemoryService facade with per-user and tenant namespacing and semantic search. embeddings.py provides the vector embeddings (an OpenAI-compatible client or a deterministic hash fallback), and pg.py is the shared async Postgres connection pool underneath both. The agent graph injects relevant long-term memories into each turn's system context.
languageLesson: pgvector extends Postgres with a vector type and ANN indexes so semantic search (ORDER BY embedding <-> query_embedding) runs in the same database that holds the relational and checkpointer state, removing the need for a separate vector database.

title: MCP & A2A Protocol Integrations
description: Self-Agent speaks two agent protocols, in both directions. On the MCP (Model Context Protocol) side, mcp/client.py loads external MCP server definitions from JSON and aggregates their tools into the agent's registry, while mcp/server.py exposes the agent's own built-in tools to other agents over stdio or HTTP/SSE via FastMCP. On the A2A (Agent-to-Agent) side, a2a/executor.py wraps the LangGraph agent as a remotely-invokable task, and a2a/client.py delegates messages to peer agents behind an SSRF-guarded URL allowlist. Together these let the agent both consume external capabilities and be composed into multi-agent systems.

title: Hermes Self-Evolution
description: Hermes is the project's self-improvement loop. memory_learner.py runs passively after each conversation: it asks the LLM to extract the user's interests, preferences, and facts, then persists them via the profile and memory services from Step 7. reflector.py is the active half: it pulls recent successful conversations, asks the LLM to critique and rewrite the current system prompt, scores the candidate, and auto-adopts the new version when the score clears a configurable threshold. prompt_store.py is the file-backed, versioned store that keeps full history so any change can be rolled back. It is async, opt-in, and every adoption is auditable.

title: API & HTTP Surface
description: The FastAPI HTTP layer exposes everything built so far. api/routes.py is the primary router and the highest-fan-out file in the codebase, mounting 26 endpoints across chat, memory, profile, sessions, history, evolution, and admin, including the three chat variants: blocking POST /chat, SSE POST /chat/stream for browsers, and NDJSON POST /chat/http-stream for the CLI. api/schemas.py defines the Pydantic request and response contract. Each streaming endpoint is what the agent graph's stream_agent generator feeds into, emitting token, tool_call, tool_start, tool_result, and done events.

title: Authentication & Multi-Tenancy
description: This is what makes the service enterprise-grade. jwt_service.py issues and verifies JWTs with bcrypt password hashing and admin-role detection. dependencies.py provides the FastAPI Depends hooks (CurrentUser resolution, admin enforcement, and owner versus anonymous access guards) that protect every endpoint from Step 10. tenant.py implements multi-tenant isolation: an unforgeable tenant_id resolved server-side from request headers namespaces every user, thread, and memory id, so tenants sharing the same database cannot see each other's data. Notably these are cross-cutting concerns layered on top; the core agent code is untouched by them.
languageLesson: FastAPI dependency injection (Depends) resolves per-request values like the authenticated user before the route body runs, and dependencies can themselves depend on other dependencies, so the auth chain (header to token to user to tenant) composes naturally and fails fast with a 401 or 403.

title: Client Applications
description: Two deliverable clients consume the service. On the web side, App.jsx is the React chat shell (auth gating, sessions, tool-step rendering, and SSE consumption) and api.js is its HTTP/SSE client, managing JWTs in localStorage and hand-parsing the SSE stream via ReadableStream. On the CLI side, selfagent_cli/main.py is the Rich-powered interactive REPL and command dispatcher, and local.py is the architectural alternative: it runs the agent in-process with no HTTP backend, presetting environment variables before any app import, registering tools, and warming the compiled graph. Local mode is what makes this a coding agent that works directly on your disk rather than just a chat server.

title: Infrastructure & Data Stack
description: The tour closes with what runs underneath everything. docker-compose.yml brings up the five-service stack (pgvector Postgres, MongoDB, Redis, Jaeger for tracing, and Neo4j for the user-profile graph) with health checks and persistent volumes. infra/postgres/init.sql is the schema bootstrap: it installs the pgcrypto, pg_trgm, and vector extensions and creates the tenant-scoped users and conversations tables that the memory and auth layers depend on. The .env.example template is the canonical 67-setting manifest; copy it to .env and every field flows into app/core/config.py from Step 2 to configure the entire system.
languageLesson: docker-compose orchestration: depends_on with healthchecks, named volumes for persistence, and container init scripts (mongo/init.js, postgres/init.sql) that auto-run on first start let the whole multi-service stack come up reproducibly with a single command.
